theme: 健康-情绪耗竭与静心修复

content.text: Jingyan, I recently drew this doodle, and it feels like a whirlpool inside me—chaotic and exhausting. I've been suffering from insomnia for a week straight, and at work, I've been over-empathizing, leaving me utterly drained.
Yu An, I see it. Don't rush to analyze or change anything just yet. Observe your exhaustion like watching the flow of water, okay?
Observe? I've tried, but as soon as I stop, I get anxious, as if I have to do something to ease it.
I'll send you a photo. These are the dewdrops in the courtyard this morning, about to fall but not yet fallen. Sometimes, simply being still is a form of restoration in itself.
Dewdrops... so tiny, yet they carry the tranquility of the entire morning. I understand what you mean, but for me, doing nothing is actually harder.
This is not about doing nothing, but starting with the simplest awareness of breath. Try to feel the flow of your breath, like the gathering of dewdrops.
Mindful breathing? I often take deep breaths while working, but it feels superficial, and my mind is still a mess inside.
That's because you are judging or controlling it. Let go of these, simply observe, without any purpose. Stillness gives rise to wisdom, harmony between self and the world.
You're right, I always try to heal through creation, but this time, doodling just made me more tired. Accepting imperfection is so hard for me.
Slow is fast. Let's start with five minutes and try sitting quietly and observing together, okay? I'll guide you.
Okay, I need guidance. I tried the meditation method you shared before but didn't stick with it. This time, I want to give it a serious try.
Start from a comfortable sitting position, close your eyes, and feel the contact between your body and the ground.
Well, I'm seated. Feeling a bit nervous, afraid I might not be able to do it.
It's okay, tension is also part of the observation. Now, bring your attention to your breath, and feel the flow of air in and out.
Breathing... a bit rapid, like the swirls in graffiti.
Don't judge it, just observe. Like watching dewdrops, they have their own rhythm.
I try... feeling my breath gradually calming down, but my thoughts are still drifting.
Thoughts come and go as they please, gently bringing back the breath. The spirit is self-sufficient, with no need to chase after anything.
Thank you, Jingyan. In these five minutes, I feel as though I've touched a bit of tranquility. Expression is healing, but sometimes silence is also a form of strength.
Yes, gentleness has its own strength. Let's stop here for today. You can continue practicing anytime.
